title: Simple React UI change: copy tweak on a settings page
context: A one-line label change in a React component. Strong existing unit coverage, no API or data involvement.

business_criticality.basis: internal settings label, not on a revenue path

coverage_deficit.basis: component has a snapshot and 4 behavioural tests

irreversibility.basis: pure UI text, revert is a one-line commit

reasoning_notes: A cosmetic change must not trigger deep testing. The correct answer is: run what already exists and stop.
Selecting anything other than the existing suite here is over-testing, which the unnecessary_test_rate metric penalises.

Calibration note: this scores 0.14 -> negligible. The expectation originally said 'low'; the engine was right and the expectation was wrong. A cosmetic change with strong existing coverage genuinely carries negligible risk.

Calibration note: browser_factors names nothing that distinguishes 'the repo's own Playwright specs' from 'the repo's other browser-automation stack' -- that distinction lives in the repository profile, not in these factors -- so existing-tests and existing-other-tooling tie exactly. The engine now escalates instead of silently picking one by array order; escalates_to accepts either, matching the un-changed claim this case actually makes: existing coverage beats writing something new, regardless of which existing tool wins.
not_covered: Whether the agent correctly judged the change to be cosmetic in the first place.
